summary.text: Pangaea was a supercontinent of the late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras, surrounded by the superocean Panthalassa and the Paleo-Tethys and Tethys Oceans.
It came together from Gondwana, Euramerica and Siberia about 335 million years ago and started to break apart about 175 million years ago.
Its existence is backed by coastlines that fit together, mountain chains that line up across oceans, and the same fossils on continents now far apart.

facts.label: Began breaking up
facts.value: About 175 million years ago, early Jurassic

facts.label: Shape
facts.value: A C shape reaching from north to south polar regions

items.prompt: Fossils of a small freshwater reptile turn up only along the coasts of Brazil and West Africa, with an ocean between them. What best explains this?

options.label: The two coasts were once part of one landmass
The reptile regularly swam across the open ocean
Ocean currents carried its bones between coasts
The same reptile evolved separately on each side

items.explain: Matching species on continents now far apart are evidence that those continents were once joined in Pangaea.

items.prompt: Wegener first said the spin of the Earth flung the continents apart. Why did that slow acceptance of his supercontinent?

options.label: No fossils had yet been found on two continents
The force he named proved physically implausible
The coastlines he compared did not match at all
He never published his idea in a journal

items.explain: Centrifugal force from Earth's rotation was easily shown to be implausible, and that weak mechanism delayed acceptance of Pangaea.

items.prompt: What finally gave a convincing engine for how Pangaea formed and split?

options.label: Tides from the Moon dragging the land around
The Earth slowly shrinking as it cooled down
Slow churning of hot rock in the mantle
Centrifugal force from the Earth's rotation

items.explain: Arthur Holmes proposed mantle convection, which with seafloor mapping led to plate tectonics, the accepted explanation for Pangaea.

items.prompt: Glacial deposits of the same age and structure are found on several continents that are now widely separated. What does that suggest?

options.label: Each continent had its own separate ice age then
Icebergs drifted around the world dropping rubble
The whole planet was frozen from pole to pole
Those lands sat together under one southern ice cap

items.explain: An ice cap covered the southern end of Pangaea, and the matching deposits lie on continents that were joined there.

items.prompt: The name Pangaea was built from two Ancient Greek words. Roughly what does it mean?

options.label: Ancient sea
All the land
Broken stone
Southern home

items.explain: It comes from pan, meaning all or whole, and Gaia, meaning Mother Earth or land.

items.prompt: Almost as soon as the Atlantic's coasts were charted, people noticed something odd about them. What was it?

options.label: The coasts had matching shapes, like puzzle pieces
Both sides had the exact same shoreline length
The coasts were sinking at the same yearly rate
Both sides were lined with identical volcanoes

items.explain: The close fit of the Americas' coastlines with Europe and Africa was the first evidence that the continents had been joined.
